items.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025
items.q: She was Carole and Gerry’s house sitter. Took care of the kids.

ctx.x: You just said an important thing about — I translate it as it’s not necessary for you to really like something in order to do a good job with it. That you don’t have to love a piece of music to give it your all, and to be professional.

No. But I can hardly remember pieces that I didn’t like. There was one demo I did which was a sort of an oddball thing from some other studio. And I think it was Liberace’s brother had a company that said, “We’ll set your song to music.” So people would send in lyrics and they would put them to the same damn tune that was awful. That one stands out in my mind because all the rest of them I did were for the real pros. And those who weren’t pros became pros, like Little Eva you know, Eva, “Locomotion.” She was…
I wonder if you ever had an experience where you did a demo and you said to yourself, “This is going to be a hit.” You recognized it as the potential.
